The community of Mariposa gathered this week for the Highway 140 Centennial Celebration – the all-weather entrance to Yosemite National Park. In the darkest days of the Civil War, President Lincoln signed the Yosemite Grant Act, which contained an extraordinary promise: that it shall be held for public use, resort, and recreation…inalienable for all time. For a century Highway 140 has fulfilled that promise. It was an honor to help commemorate the occasion.

The greater Yosemite community’s thoughts remain with the helicopter crew lost battling the Dome Fire in Yosemite.  Ryan Cutter and Greg King came here to protect our community and our nation’s most treasured national wonder and they gave their lives in doing so. I am grateful to all those fighting the fire, and to the fire command and Mariposa Sheriff’s Office for providing me an update.

Statement by the Congressional Iran Human Rights and Democracy Caucus:  As reports indicate that Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian plans to attend the 81st United Nations General Assembly, the Congressional Iran Human Rights and Democracy Caucus urges the international community not to ignore the regime's worsening human rights record.

While Tehran seeks to present a moderate face at the United Nations, the reality for the Iranian people is continued repression. Human rights organizations report that more than 4,100 executions have been carried out under Pezeshkian's tenure, including political prisoners, protesters, and members of ethnic and religious minorities.

The Iranian regime's principal war is not with foreign adversaries. Its primary war is against its own people. Executions, torture, arbitrary arrests, sham trials, and suppression of free expression remain the regime's tools of control.

As President Pezeshkian addresses world leaders in New York, we call on the United States and its allies to publicly condemn these abuses, support international accountability efforts, and ensure that human rights remain central to all engagement with Iran.

We stand with the Iranian people and the thousands of Iranian Americans from more than 40 states who support a free, secular, democratic, and non-nuclear republic in Iran. The voices of those executed, imprisoned, and silenced must not be forgotten.
